config.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala

personas.name: Celeste
personas.goals: A gala worthy of the orchestra's reputation
personas.hidden_agenda: The withdrawn sponsor is her brother-in-law's firm

personas.name: Rafael
personas.hidden_agenda: Already drafted a smaller backup plan

personas.name: Nkechi
personas.goals: Keep the night joyful for the kids

personas.name: Howard
personas.goals: Nobody spends money we don't have
personas.hidden_agenda: Warned the board about relying on one big sponsor

agenda.title: Budget adjustments
agenda.goal: Decide what to cut or change

agenda.title: Performance program
agenda.goal: Settle the student program for the night

agenda.title: Ticket push
agenda.goal: Agree how to sell the remaining seats

facts.statement: Scholarships funded by last year's gala = 22

beats.summary: How bad it is; Celeste inflates the loss and gets corrected
Cuts; the catering figure; Rafael's backup plan; a long detour about Vienna
The student program; who plays and how long
Selling the rest; Nkechi's count is high and is corrected later

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Thank you for joining at short notice. Hartwell Partners has pulled out. We've lost forty thousand dollars, just like that.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Twenty-five. Their pledge was twenty-five thousand. I have the letter in front of me.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Twenty-five, forty, it's a catastrophe either way.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: To be candid, it's serious, but it isn't a catastrophe. We still have four sponsors.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Did they say why they pulled out?

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Something about a restructuring. I don't know the details.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Does the press know yet?

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: I said at the board retreat that one sponsor was a third of our income. Nobody wanted to hear it.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Howard, this isn't the moment for I-told-you-so.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: It's exactly the moment. Otherwise we do it again next year.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Can we focus on what we can control?

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: My train's going into a tunnel, I might cut out for a minute.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: What's the revenue goal still, with this hole in it?

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: One hundred and fifty thousand, on paper. Realistically, less.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Last year we netted a hundred and fifty, so the goal is not crazy.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: The goal stays as it is for now. We'll see where the budget lands.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: The budget. Howard?

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Forty-six thousand budgeted. We've committed about thirty so far.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: The biggest line is catering. It's ninety-five a head.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Eighty-five. It's eighty-five a head, with the wine.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Eighty-five. Right, ninety-five was the first quote.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: We are not serving people sandwiches at a gala.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Nobody's saying sandwiches. A plated dinner without the third course, maybe?

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: The third course is the dessert. The dessert is the part people remember.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Fair enough.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: When I was in Vienna last spring, the opera ball had seven courses. Seven.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: I'm sure it did.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: And a waltz between every one. The children there learn to waltz at ten.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Our children learn the Bach double concerto at ten. That's better than a waltz.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: To be candid, I drafted a smaller version of the gala last night, just in case.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Of course you did.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Same venue, no printed program, digital auction catalog, and the string quartet instead of hiring a band. It saves about nine thousand.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: That's real money.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: The band was the best part last year.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: The kids are the best part. The quartet is the kids.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Fine. The quartet, then. And the digital catalog. But we keep the dessert.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: I can live with that.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: I'll send the revised budget to the board tonight.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Send it to me first, please.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Of course. You first, then the board.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Sorry, my signal was patchy through all of that. Where did we land?

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: We cut the band. The quartet will play.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Good. Then the program. Sixty students are performing in total.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Sixty is wonderful, but the program can't run longer than forty minutes. People start leaving.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Is there a way to let every section play something?

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: The full orchestra opens, then three short ensembles, then the soloist. Everyone plays at least once.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Who's the soloist this year?

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Mei-Lin, the cellist. She won the regional competition.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Then Mei-Lin closes the program. It's settled.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Somebody needs to talk to the venue about the stage size for the full orchestra.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: I've measured it twice. It fits if the timpani go stage left.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Excuse me. Frog in my throat.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Tickets. How many have we sold?

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: About two hundred and fifty. It's going really well.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Excellent. Then we're nearly full.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Out of three hundred seats.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: At a hundred seventy-five a ticket, every remaining seat matters.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: Could the parents of the performers sell tickets to their own families?

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: They already get two free tickets each. That's part of the problem.

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: Then we ask each family to bring one paying guest. That's the ask.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: I have the box office report open. It's a hundred and eighty-eight sold, not two fifty.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: Oh. I counted the free family tickets. Sorry.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: A hundred and eighty-eight. Then we need that ask more than ever.

turns.speaker: Nkechi
turns.text: I'll write to all the performer families tomorrow morning about the paying guest.

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: And mention the scholarships. Twenty-two students last year.

turns.speaker: Howard
turns.text: Who's going to ask Hartwell if they'd still buy a table?

turns.speaker: Rafael
turns.text: The date hasn't moved, has it? Still the twelfth?

turns.speaker: Celeste
turns.text: April twelfth. It never moves. Thank you all. We'll get through this.
